comment: Phase [A2.25] hand-seeded 50 manual edges: top-star Azure AI accelerators -> matched FrootAI Solution Plays. Source: github:pavle. Every edge has source=manual (vs auto from A2.5 LLM suggester or community_pr from override files A2.24). Every confidence >= 0.75 (well above A2.16 MIN_CONFIDENCE_FOR_BUNDLE=0.7). Reasons cite specific overlap: README content, tech stack, IaC, pattern lineage. See frootai/orchard/registry/pollinations.json README and planning/fai-orchard-masterplan.md A2.25.

edges.reason: This accelerator IS the canonical Azure AI Search + Azure OpenAI hybrid-retrieval reference that Play 01 codifies as a Solution Play. Same Bicep, same azd template, same Container Apps topology, same hybrid+vector retrieval pattern.
Play 09 offers a portal-oriented variant of the same search foundation. Use Play 09 when the UX is search-results-first; use this accelerator when chat-first with grounded citations.
Play 21 layers tool-using agents on top of the same retrieval substrate this accelerator establishes - agent picks the right index/filter per query instead of fixed hybrid scoring.

Semantic Kernel's Planner + Plugin/Function model is the canonical primitive Play 03's deterministic-agent pattern wraps. Plays that need bounded tool-calling with audit logs default to SK as the runtime.
SK's Agent Framework (AgentChat + GroupChatManager) directly implements the multi-agent collaboration loop Play 22 specifies - same handoff + termination semantics.
Play 07's service-shaped multi-agent endpoint deploys most naturally on top of SK's Agent + AgentChat primitives with the SK Process Framework for long-running orchestrations.
AutoGen (and its Magentic-One showcase) IS the multi-agent swarm pattern Play 22 codifies - same role specialisation, group-chat manager, and consensus-via-conversation primitives.
Play 07's hosted multi-agent service maps cleanly to AutoGen's runtime + bench harness; team-of-agents is the same conceptual primitive.
GraphRAG IS the upstream canonical implementation of Play 28's knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval pattern. Same community-detection, hierarchical summaries, and local/global query modes.
GPT-RAG is the enterprise-hardened evolution of Play 01: same retrieve-rerank-generate core, but adds private endpoints, AAD-only auth, App Gateway WAF, and per-tenant isolation.

GPT-RAG's networking + identity Bicep modules (private endpoints, AAD, Key Vault) implement Play 11's advanced landing-zone primitives end-to-end; reusable as the infra layer for any L7 enterprise RAG.
Both ship a search-grounded chat surface; GPT-RAG prioritises zero-trust posture, Play 09 prioritises searchable-portal UX. Pick by user need.
Lessons 03-05 of the curriculum walk through deterministic single-agent patterns (Plan to Tool-call to Verify) that directly mirror Play 03's contract.
Lessons 07-09 cover multi-agent collaboration with AutoGen - Play 22's pattern implemented in runnable notebook form.
10-lesson agents curriculum IS the canonical Microsoft Learn realisation of Play 65's training-curriculum pattern. Same lesson-then-runnable-notebook structure.
The agents directory ships runnable Foundry-hosted deterministic-agent samples (tool-calling + thread state) that match Play 03's pattern step-for-step.
The prompts and prompt-flow directories demonstrate the prompt-versioning + A/B-evaluation surface Play 18 standardises.
The evaluation samples wire Foundry's built-in evaluators + golden datasets in the exact shape Play 98 specifies for an agent-evaluation platform.
One-click deployment wrapper for Microsoft GraphRAG on Container Apps - IS Play 28's deployable instantiation for Azure.
Both solve enterprise RAG over Azure but use a different retrieval substrate (graph vs hybrid+vector). Pick GraphRAG when relationships drive ranking; pick Play 01 when text relevance does.
PromptFlow IS the upstream tool Play 18 wraps for prompt-versioning, batch-eval, and trace inspection. Same flow.dag.yaml + run.yaml primitives.
PromptFlow's built-in evaluators (relevance, groundedness, fluency) + the eval-comparison UI fulfil Play 98's evaluation-platform contract directly.
PromptFlow's tool-node + LLM-node graph compiles to a deterministic agent execution suitable as Play 03's runtime layer (vs SK as the alternative).
Magentic-One is the canonical multi-agent swarm reference (Orchestrator + WebSurfer + FileSurfer + Coder + Terminal) - literally the worked example of Play 22.
Magentic-One's WebSurfer agent uses the Playwright-driven browser-automation pattern Play 23 codifies; same DOM observation + action loop.
OmniParser provides the screenshot-to-clickable-elements parser that IS Play 42's computer-use-agent perception layer - every computer-use agent needs this primitive.
Browser-only variants of Play 23 use OmniParser to convert page screenshots into structured DOM-action targets without DOM access.
Solution accelerator competitor to Play 01's reference; same conversational-RAG goal but with Speech integration + Power Virtual Agents bot framework defaults.
Its Speech-to-Text + bot routing layer overlaps Play 05's IT-ticket support-agent pattern; can be retrofitted for ticket workflows.
PromptFlow-centric RAG reference solving the same enterprise grounded-chat goal as Play 01; pick this when PromptFlow tooling is the deployment vehicle, Play 01 when azd is.
Contoso-Chat's flow.dag.yaml + variant configuration is a worked example of Play 18's prompt-management pattern at production scale.
Samples include grounded-chat-with-citation notebooks demonstrating Play 01's retrieve-rerank-generate primitives in runnable form.
Includes function-calling and Foundry-agent samples that demonstrate Play 03's bounded tool-using-agent pattern.
Same Play 01 RAG goal but pgvector + PostgreSQL instead of Azure AI Search. Pick when the org already runs Postgres and wants to avoid a new search service line-item.
Reference baseline that builds out the same RAG architecture as Play 01 but adds App Service hosting, AKS-equivalent compute alternatives, and a fully-documented architecture decision record.
Its hub-and-spoke networking + Key Vault + Log Analytics Bicep is a working Play 02 landing-zone - reusable as the infra layer for any AOAI workload.
Document-ingestion-into-AI-Search reference; overlaps Play 09's search-portal pattern at the index-build layer. Pick for ingestion-heavy use cases.
Code-first agent runtime that solves the same single-deterministic-agent contract as Play 03 (Plan to Code to Execute to Verify) with a Python-centric API.
TaskWeaver's role-experts + planner architecture is a leaner alternative to AutoGen for Play 22's multi-agent collaboration when domain experts are the unit of decomposition.
Catalog of vector + hybrid + semantic ranker recipes that fulfil Play 09's portal-search retrieval substrate (any of these recipes plugs in as the index strategy).
Same recipes are reusable as the Play 26 semantic-search-engine retrieval core; hybrid+semantic ranking is the primitive.
Demonstrates AKS Bicep + KEDA autoscaling + Service Mesh that Play 12's AKS model-serving topology needs as its foundation layer.
Hands-on workshop that walks through every Play 01 primitive (ingestion, indexing, retrieval, prompt-grounding) in lab-by-lab form.
Multi-lab structure with progressive exercises is the Play 65 training-curriculum pattern applied to RAG specifically.
Constraint-driven generation DSL solves prompt-management's structured-output side of Play 18 differently than PromptFlow's flow-graph approach.
LIDA's grammar-guided synthetic dataset generation is a worked instance of Play 47's synthetic-data-factory pattern (target schema then seeded LLM then validated rows).
Foundry-centric landing-zone deployment IS the canonical realisation of Play 02 for the Azure AI Foundry product line: hub + project + connected resources, AAD-only.
Pre-wires Application Insights + Foundry tracing + Log Analytics workbooks, fulfilling Play 17's observability instrumentation contract end-to-end.
Microsoft Industry Solutions enterprise-RAG accelerator extends Play 01's baseline with FHIR + claims-data adapters specifically; same core, hardened for healthcare data.
Implements Play 30's hardening pattern (private endpoints + customer-managed keys + audit logging + AAD-only) in production-ready Bicep modules.
